extracted.intended_audience: prospective Fulbright applicants (U.S. students, non-students, artists, professors/administrators, non-U.S. applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Official home-page guidance on who may apply to the Fulbright U.S. Student Program, which award tracks are available, deadlines, and where different applicant types should apply or seek help (FPAs, Fulbright Commission, fulbrightscholars.org).

rubrics_metrics.name: Current U.S. Student eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: United States citizens who are currently enrolled in undergraduate or graduate degree programs are eligible to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are currently enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate program at a U.S. college or university, you will apply through that institution, even if you are not currently a resident there. Find the Fulbright Program Adviser on your campus.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. Citizen (not currently a student) eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are a U.S. citizen, will hold a bachelor’s degree by the award start date, and do not have a Ph.D. degree, then you are eligible to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-enrolled applicants should have relatively limited professional experience in the fields (typically 7 years or less) in which they are applying. Candidates with more experience should consider applying for the Fulbright Scholar Program. The Getting Started page provides information on eligibility and next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artist (creative & performing arts) eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fulbright U.S. Student Program welcomes applications in the creative and performing arts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arts candidates for the U.S. Student Program should have relatively limited professional experience in the fields (typically 7 years or less) in which they are applying. Artists with more experience should consider applying for the Fulbright Scholar Program. Creative & Performing Arts projects fall under the Study/Research grant category and are available in all countries where Study/Research grants are offered.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. Professor/Administrator application route
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. citizens who are professors or administrators and interested in a Fulbright Scholar Award must use a different application channel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are a U.S. citizen and a professor or administrator at a U.S. institution and are interested in applying for a Fulbright Scholar Award, you will need to apply through fulbrightscholars.org. To support your students in applying for a U.S. Student Program award, please connect with the Fulbright Program Adviser at your institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-U.S. citizen applicants to the United States
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-U.S. citizens interested in applying for a Fulbright Award to the United States must apply through their home-country offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You will need to apply through the Fulbright Commission or U.S. Embassy in your home country. Find out more information on the Fulbright Visiting Scholar Program or Fulbright Foreign Student Program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application tracks / types of awards
rubrics_metrics.description: The U.S. Student Program offers multiple award types and specialty programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed award types include Study/Research Awards, English Teaching Assistant (ETA) Awards, Fulbright‑National Geographic Award Program, and Fulbright‑Fogarty Fellowships in Public Health. Applicants should choose the award type that matches their project or field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study/Research — Academic component
rubrics_metrics.description: Study/Research grants have an academic track for research- or study-focused proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 'Study/Research: Academic' application component for specifics (linked from the site). Academic Study/Research awards are one of the primary application tracks for U.S. Student applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study/Research — Creative & Performing Arts component
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative & Performing Arts projects are handled within the Study/Research grant category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artists and creative practitioners should apply under the 'Study/Research: Creative & Performing Arts' component; these projects are available in all countries where Study/Research grants are offered.

rubrics_metrics.name: English Teaching Assistant (ETA) component
rubrics_metrics.description: The ETA award is a distinct application component focused on teaching English abroad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective applicants interested in teaching English should consult the ETA application component for eligibility, expectations, and application requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines and competition timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Competition cycles and important dates govern eligibility and application submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the 2027–2028 Award Cycle the application is now open; the National Deadline is Tuesday, October 6, 2026 at 5 pm Eastern Time. For the 2026–2027 Award Cycle the application is closed and final notifications are on a rolling basis through spring. Applicants must adhere to stated national deadlines and competition timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find and consult a Fulbright Program Adviser (FPA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are encouraged/expected to connect with an institutional adviser for guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find the Fulbright Program Adviser on your campus (Search FPA). FPAs provide guidance, and institutions are the application route for enrolled U.S. students.
